morphology.motility: Motile via a single polar flagellum

habitat.hostAssociation: Free-living marine organism; opportunistic foodborne pathogen when ingested via seafood
habitat.environmentalOccurrence: Halophilic (requires salt); common in warm coastal waters, concentrates in shellfish

culture.growthCharacteristics: Halophilic — requires added NaCl to grow; does not grow well without salt
culture.colonyMorphology: Green colonies on TCBS agar (does not ferment sucrose, unlike V. cholerae which is yellow)
culture.hemolysis: Beta-hemolytic on special blood agar (Kanagawa phenomenon in pathogenic strains)

identificationClues: Halophilic — will not grow on media without added salt
Green (sucrose-negative) colonies on TCBS agar, unlike the yellow (sucrose-positive) V. cholerae
Kanagawa phenomenon (beta-hemolysis on a special blood agar) correlates with pathogenic strains
History of raw or undercooked seafood/shellfish consumption

diseases: Acute gastroenteritis (watery or occasionally bloody diarrhea)
Wound infections after exposure to seawater
Rarely, septicemia in immunocompromised or cirrhotic patients
virulenceFactors: Thermostable direct hemolysin (TDH, responsible for the Kanagawa phenomenon)
clinicalImportance.transmission: Ingestion of raw or undercooked seafood, particularly oysters; wound contamination from seawater exposure
clinicalImportance.epidemiology: A leading cause of seafood-associated bacterial gastroenteritis worldwide, particularly in coastal and island regions with high raw-seafood consumption
clinicalImportance.labSignificance: Halophilic growth requirement and green TCBS colonies distinguish it from V. cholerae at the bench before confirmatory biochemical/serologic testing

examFacts.distinguishingFeature: Requires added salt to grow, unlike V. cholerae
